findings.reason: The protected solution is compact, conventional, and interview-ready. The destination, direction, position, volume, and heights names expose the simulation state and directional search directly; no generic local named index obscures a semantic role.

For each droplet, destination starts at k. A directional scan crosses exactly the contiguous non-rising path available to the droplet and updates destination only when it encounters a strictly lower height, which retains the nearest position to k when the minimum lies on a plateau. Completing the left scan before considering the right enforces left priority; entering the right scan only when no lower left destination exists enforces the fallback rule. If neither side is lower, destination remains k. Incrementing the chosen cell before the next iteration faithfully incorporates every earlier droplet into the terrain seen by later droplets.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 755, Python, and the native pourWater(heights, volume, k) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms unit-width terrain columns, sequential unit droplets poured at k, left-before-right eventual-fall preference, fallback at k, level as terrain plus settled water, infinitely high out-of-bounds walls, and indivisible water units. It also confirms 1 through 100 columns, initial heights from 0 through 99, volume from 0 through 2000, and every valid k.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065954247 are algorithmically identical: both process one droplet at a time, initialize destination at k, scan left then right across the same non-rising condition, retain only strict height improvements, stop after a successful left search, increment the selected position, and return the mutated heights list. Their only structural differences are the required Solution.pourWater wrapper and Python typing dialect.

The unchanged three authored workloads grow ascending terrains from 8 to 32 positions with four droplets poured at the right boundary, forcing direct directional traversal across the terrain while candidate-by-candidate path validation performs quadratic work in terrain length. The exact protected source passed all twelve visible correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent +0.02 and a 1.00x largest runtime ratio. A structurally independent direct-scan implementation also passed, with exponent +0.02 and a 1.04x largest ratio. A correct path-revalidation control matched every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.77, distinguishing O(vn) direct simulation from O(vn^2) path revalidation.

The Approach accurately derives non-rising directional reachability, strict destination updates for nearest-plateau behavior, left priority, fallback at k, and the need to mutate after each droplet. Its O(vn) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The modular Reference preserves the unit-width terrain model, sequential indivisible droplets, ordered left/right/stay rules, eventual-fall and level definitions, infinitely high boundary walls, all three source examples, both source explanations, and all four constraints. Five accessible stage tables reproduce the complete terrain-versus-water state carried by the five source diagrams for Example 1.

Authenticated live Premium evidence confirms exactly three examples in source order, explanations for Examples 1 and 2 only, four constraints, five sequential source diagrams, no source tables, and no hint or follow-up section. The modular Reference and every composed section are hash-bound by a verified source_fidelity.json against live statement content hash f3eb0ef37d5e85a283b02f63a9e61012784052f133cfe5ca0e11f76de0418a7d.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly three examples. Their exact height arrays, volumes, pour indices, and final arrays appear first in source order; the former trial using [3,1,3], volume 5, and k 1 is now correctly classified as source sample 3.

All twelve ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials. The former hidden single-column, barrier, and closest-minimum-plateau checks were exposed and strengthened with explicit boundary and semantic coverage.

Authored and generated checks cover terrain lengths 1 and 100, initial heights 0 and 99, volume 0 and 2000, and k at both endpoints as well as interior positions. The maximum-volume single-column trial also verifies that final water levels are not capped at the initial-height limit.

Material behavior covers sequential terrain mutation, left-before-right preference even when right also falls, right fallback, movement across equal levels toward a deeper reachable column, the nearest column on a minimum plateau, taller barriers, flat terrain, basins, and staying at k when neither direction eventually falls.

Expected results were checked against an independent semantic oracle that enumerates each direction's reachable non-rising columns and selects the nearest occurrence of its minimum level. The oracle, protected app adapter, and immutable native Solution agreed on all fifteen authored correctness-plus-benchmark inputs, 185688 exhaustive states over lengths through 6, 5000 deterministic random legal inputs, and two maximum-boundary inputs.

The unchanged 8-, 16-, and 32-column ascending-slope workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 4x, and make the correct path-revalidation control fail only the scaling verdict.
